newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Brit Steel buyback helps dull stg pain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Brit Steel buyback helps dull stg pain.

text.p: British Steel Plc launched a share buyback programme on Thursday, seeking to ease the pain inflicted on investors by sterling strength which continues to cripple profitability.
The steel giant said the repurchase programme would enhance the efficiency of its balance sheet and earnings per share.

"Essentially our balance sheet was healthy but our shares were very depressed and we thought they were also undervalued. This (buyback) enhances value for all shareholders," John Bowden, British Steel director of investor and media relations, told Reuters
Cazenove & Co, appointed by the group to handle the share repurchase, told Reuters it had been asked to buy up to 100 million shares, or five percent, at 155 pence in an initial offer.
But British Steel has shareholder authority to buy back up to 10 percent of shares from a motion passed at last year's annual shareholders' meeting.
Bowden said British Steel could make further purchases to raise its buyback to the 10 percent maximum allowed.
"There is no set timescale on this," he said.
The surprise move boosted British Steel's shares to 154 1/2 pence, up four and 3/4 pence by 1105 GMT.

The buyback comes just one month after British Steel reported a collapse in year profits to 451 million pounds ($756.3 million) from 1.1 billion the previous year thanks to the relentless rise of sterling on world currency markets.

Profits are seen falling back even further this year, with most analysts pitching in the 100 million to 200 million pounds range. At least one industry analyst is forecasting that British Steel will make a loss.
The root of British Steel's woes has been the surging pound which was buttressed by recent British interest rate hikes. Further hikes are seen in the pipeline.
In recent days sterling went over the three Deutsche mark threshold but has since eased back to 2.9900. But that's still around 30 percent higher than last summer.
The July 2 British budget hurt the shares of exporters like British Steel by raising the likelihood of more interest rate hikes and boosting the pound further.
Economists said higher interest rates would be necessary because the Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown had not done enough to curb the consumer boom.
The budget's abolition of the dividend tax credit was also seen possibly forcing companies like British Steel to pay more into their pension funds.

British Steel decided to launch the buyback against this backdrop. Bowden added that the buyback funded from its 785 million pounds in net cash "doesn't impair our overseas expansion plans or our dividend outlook."
Commenting on the outlook for trading as the pound's ascent continues unabated, Bowden said it looked like the company was in "for a protracted period of sterling strength."
"People are taking the view that partial good news on firmer underlying (steel) selling prices and cost-cutting can only partially mitigate the impact of sterling."
The group plans to give a trading update next week when it holds its annual shareholders' meeting.
($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
